page: Microsoft Azure M128ms is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8280M processors with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 38 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 3892.0 GB of system memory, yielding 30.41 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, the server includes 4194 GB of local SSD storage and is premium storage capable, but does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data highlights a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is consistently limited, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression and decompression tests falling into the bottom 10% tier. Conversely, multi-core capabilities are robust; stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression benchmarks rank in the top 25%. Memory performance is a primary strength, with uncached read-only memory bandwidth for large blocks reaching 375.19 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10% tier. Large block write bandwidth and cached small block read bandwidth also show strong performance in the top 25%.

Given its massive memory footprint and strong multi-threaded performance, the M128ms is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise-grade relational databases, and heavy data caching layers. This is supported by its strong Redis SET operations performance, which reaches 79.29 million operations per second. However, it is poorly suited for single-threaded tasks or intensive LLM text generation, where it registers poor performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density for memory-bound applications, though the lower single-core performance represents a tradeoff for compute-bound tasks.
